literatureAccess.tools: The Europe PMC REST API (curl) returned PubMed records with abstracts for every source below. WebSearch worked; one query (recent reviews on resuming running after an interruption) returned no systematic review and mostly coaching or commercial pages, which are not used. It surfaced one observational study, which I then read at abstract level through Europe PMC (L9). No full text was read. The IOC 2022 full text was not attempted again; the benchmark records HTTP 403.
literatureAccess.role: Direction only, for six questions. Is consistent partial training a stop? Is an isolated session a resumption? Does a strength gap or a missed strength session bear on running tolerance? Does strength training maintain running adaptations during a running lapse? What does a race or taper week's load show? Where does the clinical return boundary fall? Every class, recipe and ceiling used here is existing approved policy. No number is set, revised or taken from these sources.

sources.citation: Hickson RC, Rosenkoetter MA. Reduced training frequencies and maintenance of increased aerobic power. Med Sci Sports Exerc 1981. PMID 7219129
sources.use: 12 young adults: VO2max gained over 10 weeks was maintained for 15 weeks at 2 or 4 days a week, with intensity and duration kept. Weeks with most sessions done, long and quality included, are not a stop.

sources.citation: Spiering BA, Mujika I, Sharp MA, Foulis SA. Maintaining physical performance: the minimal dose of exercise needed to preserve endurance and strength over time. J Strength Cond Res 2021;35:1449-1458. PMID 33629972
sources.use: Narrative review. Endurance was maintained up to 15 weeks at as few as 2 sessions a week, or 33-66% less volume, with intensity kept. Strength and size (younger people) were maintained up to 32 weeks at 1 session a week and 1 set per exercise. Intensity is the key variable; data on athletes are insufficient.

sources.citation: Mujika I, Padilla S. Detraining Part I: short term insufficient training stimulus. Sports Med 2000. PMID 10966148
sources.use: Under 4 weeks of insufficient stimulus: rapid VO2max and blood-volume decline in highly trained athletes, more moderate in recently trained; strength declines are limited.

sources.citation: Mujika I, Padilla S. Detraining Part II: long term insufficient training stimulus. Sports Med 2000. PMID 10999420
sources.use: Over 4 weeks: marked VO2max decline. Losses can be avoided or limited by reduced training if intensity is kept and frequency only moderately reduced. Cross-training may help, but athletes should use similar-mode exercise. Counter-weight for SSCTR-P34-F04: strength work does not stand in for running.

sources.citation: Zheng J, Pan T, Jiang Y, Shen Y. Effects of short- and long-term detraining on maximal oxygen uptake in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Biomed Res Int 2022. PMID 36017396
sources.use: 21 studies: VO2max falls after short-term cessation (ES -0.62) and more after long-term cessation (ES -1.42). A longer continuous stop detrains more.

sources.citation: Houston ME, Bentzen H, Larsen H. Interrelationships between skeletal muscle adaptations and performance as studied by detraining and retraining. Acta Physiol Scand 1979. PMID 420018
sources.use: 6 well-trained runners: 15 days off cut VO2max 4% and performance time 25%; after 15 days of retraining, performance was still 9% below. A whole executed week shows tolerated dose, not restored capacity.

sources.citation: Bosquet L, Berryman N, Dupuy O, et al., Mujika I. Effect of training cessation on muscular performance: a meta-analysis. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2013. PMID 23347054
sources.use: 103 studies: resistance-training cessation reduces all strength components, by duration, training status and age. One missed session is not a cessation.

sources.citation: Schumann M, Feuerbacher JF, Sunkeler M, et al. Compatibility of concurrent aerobic and strength training for skeletal muscle size and function: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Med 2022. PMID 34757594
sources.use: 43 studies: concurrent training does not blunt maximal strength or hypertrophy against strength alone; explosive strength is attenuated. Interference concerns strength adaptation under concurrent load. It gives no basis for holding running because of a strength data gap.

sources.citation: Feely C, Smyth B, Caulfield B, Lawlor A. Estimating the cost of training disruptions on marathon performance. Front Sports Act Living 2022. PMID 36704260
sources.use: Observational: about 300,000 recreational marathoners. Complete cessations of 7 days or more cost 5-8% finish time against the same runners' undisrupted marathons. It is complete cessation, not reduced training, that is costly.

sources.citation: Lauersen JB, Andersen TE, Andersen LB. Strength training as superior, dose-dependent and safe prevention of acute and overuse sports injuries: a systematic review, qualitative analysis and meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med 2018. PMID 30131332
sources.use: Counter-evidence for Q3. Six RCTs, RR 0.338; a 10% increase in strength-training volume reduced injury risk by more than 4 percentage points. A chronic, programme-level, group effect; it does not show that a missed strength session or unlogged reps in reserve raises acute running risk.

sources.citation: Bosquet L, Montpetit J, Arvisais D, Mujika I. Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007. PMID 17762369
sources.use: 27 studies: the most effective taper reduces volume 41-60% over about 2 weeks while intensity and frequency are kept. A race-week's easy runs carry a reduced load; its specific stimuli are the key sessions (Q4).

sources.citation: Ardern CL, Glasgow P, Schneiders A, et al. 2016 Consensus statement on return to sport from the First World Congress in Sports Physical Therapy, Bern. Br J Sports Med 2016. PMID 27226389
sources.use: Return to sport is a continuum alongside recovery and rehabilitation, decided ideally collaboratively by clinicians, athletes and coaches; research evidence for return decisions is scarce (Q8).

sources.citation: Schwellnus M, Adami PE, Bougault V, et al. IOC consensus statement on acute respiratory illness in athletes part 1: acute respiratory infections. Br J Sports Med 2022. PMID 35863871
sources.accessed: abstract only; full text not read
sources.use: A clinician-facing consensus that includes return-to-sport guidelines for respiratory infection. Read only as scope: return after illness is a clinical decision. No staging, criterion or duration is taken.

sources.citation: Rambaud AJM, Ardern CL, Thoreux P, Regnaux JP, Edouard P. Criteria for return to running after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: a scoping review. Br J Sports Med 2018. PMID 29720478
sources.use: 201 studies, mostly time-based criteria. Best evidence recommends clinical and performance criteria with time. Return-to-running criteria after injury are clinical, condition-specific instruments (Q8).

literatureAccess.notRead: No full text. Bickel 2011 and Nielsen 2014 (cited in SSCTR-R7D-P33-RECHECK-r1) were not re-read and are not relied on. The F08 benchmark's vendor pages were not re-read; they are a UX reference only. The search for a recent systematic review on resuming running after an interruption found none.

claimStatus.claim: Weeks in which most planned sessions are executed, long and quality runs included, at the prescribed intensity, are not physiologically a continuation of a stop. Counting them as stop days overstates detraining. This is the premise of direction A and the severity of SSCTR-P34-F03.
claimStatus.limits: Maintenance and reduced-training studies plus one observational cohort. Group means. Abstracts only. Supports no adherence count or threshold.

claimStatus.claim: One or a few sessions in a long gap do not interrupt detraining. The continuous-span reading of isolated training stays the conservative reading, so a trigger by any executed session (ANY) is rejected.
claimStatus.limits: By contrast with maintenance doses. Reaffirms SSCTR-R7D-P33-RECHECK-r1 claim 1.

claimStatus.claim: A whole executed week shows tolerance of the executed dose, not restored capacity.
claimStatus.limits: One small study, abstract only. The tolerance standard is the existing approved rule.

claimStatus.claim: A strength data gap (unlogged reps or reps in reserve) or a missed strength session carries no information about running tolerance. No scientific dependency justifies holding the running conclusion for it.
claimStatus.limits: L10 is counter-evidence at programme level (strength volume and injury risk). It is handled because the gamma outcome's combined load never exceeds the executed combination, and strength stays in the plan. It does not justify an acute coupling.

claimStatus.claim: During a running lapse, strength training does not maintain running-specific adaptations. A running lapse while strength continues is a running detraining.
claimStatus.limits: Direction only. It grades SSCTR-P34-F04 as a less-conservative residual for running, bounded by the existing single-run ceiling. It sets no rule.

claimStatus.claim: A race week's prescribed load is a reduced load whose specific stimuli are its key sessions (race touch, race). Its easy runs alone are evidence comparable to isolated sessions, not a re-entry.
claimStatus.limits: The taper meta-analysis supports only the reduced-volume, kept-intensity structure. The Q4 ruling rests mainly on the plan's own key/essential/optional labels and on the accepted direction-B rule that isolated sessions are not a re-entry.

claimStatus.claim: Return to sport after injury or illness is a clinical, condition-specific, collaborative decision; its criteria are clinical instruments with scarce evidence.
claimStatus.limits: Used only to place the Q8 boundary. No criterion is taken.

Q1_DirectionAUnderExistingAuthority.verdict: Reading x as its own return is a correct implementation of the Founder's direction A under existing authority. That means its own stop and class, the unchanged recipe with no current demonstration, its point the day after x ended, the training after it read by the evidence reducer per sport, and the later stop classed by its own days. The point is the day after x's last day. It is not the report that kept x, and not the first executed session after x.
existingAuthorityUsed: R6-NONCLINICAL-RETURN: the class table (operational.return shortMaxDays, moderateMaxDays) and the recipe (returnStrength; MODERATE re-entry from the reviewed entry dose; LONG restart with run history cleared; walk/jog ladder), unchanged

The evidence reducer (state model contract; SSCTR S-A; R7-A final P5; per sport, SSCTR R40; I10/I11): a closed or complete week steps; anything else is a fact; adverse responses hold; executed doses cap (historicalRun, SSCTR F4, QE-R7ADA-02)
R7-A final section 4 and C5: a late return's point is set back to its break's week, and the sessions before the point in that week belong to the plan before the break
The episode rule (afterReentry, interruptionEpisode, stateAtBreak from the latest return in force; R7-A final I2/I4): a later break is read from the earlier return's state
Direction B (Phase 3.3; SSCTR-R7D-P33-RECHECK-r1): the reducer's complete test, every sport, continuity for isolated training; separate breaks keep their identities (I9)

bindingReading.BR-Q1.1_scope: A return that reads separate breaks recorded and not applied (ctx.separate). Every break is screened first, unchanged: a clinical reason routes to CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED; an unclear or missing reason, or facts out of range, is ASK. The loop runs from the latest earlier break to the earliest, as now. OVERLAPS and TOUCHES are unchanged.
bindingReading.BR-Q1.2_order: For each earlier break x that neither overlaps nor touches the current stop (its first day S, and its stated start time when given), the steps run in this order. (a) Candidate weeks: plan weeks whose every live session (with a prescription and not SKIPPED) falls after x's last day and before S. A session on S itself counts only under BR-Q5. (b) FULL RE-ENTRY, unchanged: a candidate week is re-entry-complete (BR-Q4) in every sport that week plans. Then x is TRAINING_AFTER with reentryWeek, and the stop is read as now. (c) Otherwise, planned sessions between x and S with no report are asked first (TRAINING_BETWEEN_BREAKS), unchanged. (d) Otherwise, if no applied return lies between x and S, and some candidate week is re-entry-complete in at least one sport, x is OWN_RETURN under BR-Q1.3. (e) Otherwise continuity, unchanged: TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED when training is recorded between them, NO_TRAINING_BETWEEN otherwise; the stop runs through x. (f) An applied return between x and S: nothing is reconstructed, and the existing path and its question stand (QE-R7D-P33-03 residual).
bindingReading.BR-Q1.3_ownReturn: x's own stop is x together with the remaining earlier breaks, read by these same rules recursively; a decision met inside it (clinical, ASK) is returned. Its class comes from its own stop's days by the unchanged table. Its entry comes from the unchanged recipe, applied to the state at its own stop's start (stateAtBreak with x's episode and class), with no current demonstration: the reviewed entry dose. Its point is the first day after x's last day, at 00:00 local. The evidence reducer reads it as a return in force from that point; the sessions of that week before the point belong to the plan before the break (C5). The training after it is read per sport (BR-Q3.1), and the later stop's class comes from its own days. The current stop's entry follows the unchanged recipe from the per-sport state, with this review's current demonstration if it is valid. The same-day strength ASK (at.material) is unchanged.
bindingReading.BR-Q1.4_neverRecorded: The reconstruction is a reading, never a fact. It records no REESTABLISH decision, episode, adaptation, plan change or eligibility. x's declaration, eventId and inputHash are unchanged. The return records x as OWN_RETURN with ownReturn {class, days, startDate, endDate, reentered: {RUN: the first day of the week that re-entered running or null, STRENGTH: the same for strength or null}}. A break inside x's own stop keeps its own inner label. The reason states, per sport, whether it resumes from the executed history or from x's own return. Every later recomputation of this return (staleReturn, a replay, a named correction) uses the same reading, rebuilt from the return's own record (O-03, BR-Q7.2).
bindingReading.BR-Q1.5_never: When BR-Q1.3 applies, no day between x and S is counted in any class. No missed or unexecuted session is credited, in a step or in the single-run ceiling (SSCTR-P34-F01). No dose rises above what was executed since the latest entry. x's pre-break plan is never restored by date. Eligibility is the current review's (assessed on or after the latest stop ended); no historical eligibility is inferred.
bindingReading.BR-Q1.6_point: The day after x ended is the earliest point at which x's return could apply. It is the point after which every execution is training after x. It is the existing late-return rule (R7-A final section 4) at the finest grain. The report that kept x would place the executed weeks before the point; C5 would then assign them to the pre-break plan, and the training would be ignored. That is the B1-B4 behaviour, and it re-creates the inverse defect on the late form (V5). The first executed session would let a training fact set the start. It would leave the days between x's end and that session in neither x nor the return. And it has no basis in the recipe, which keys the return to the break's declared end.

Q1_DirectionAUnderExistingAuthority.testExpectations: Reference outputs, not a frozen oracle; the fresh recheck re-derives them. X5/V1: SHORT 4; running from the executed history (LONG 75, EASY 50, the R27 easy slot 41, LONG 65); strength from x's own return (Monday lifts at the return entry; back-squat 1x7 ESTABLISH; db lifts 1x12 FROM_LOG). V2: SHORT 4; running RETURN 20/30/30/45 from x's own return; strength from the executed history (back-squat 2x8@85). V3, V5, X3, X4, I4, C4, E4 and X8 as in table 1.3 for gamma. X1, X2 and X6 unchanged from R7D-FREEZE-4. The F01 witness F1-F6, K1-K3, E1-E3 and the QRE cases are identical to R7D-FREEZE-4 in doses (E4 is relabelled OWN_RETURN at the same doses). The clinical cases (C1-C3, X7) are identical. The timely comparators V4 and K are identical. My R1/R1b/R2 cases, with the ceiling fixed, give running no higher than the episode rule on the same facts (G5: 15/20/25).

Q2_IsolatedVersusConsistentTraining.verdict: The right existing predicate is a plan week wholly between, re-entry-complete (BR-Q4) in at least one sport. ANY is rejected: it reopens the isolated-session pattern on long gaps (X1: 14 + 21 + 4 days with one run would give SHORT 4 RETURN against LONG 39 RESTART; F1-F6 relabelled; CL2). X2 staying on continuity (both sports partial every week, LONG 32 RESTART) is accepted only as a disclosed, authority-limited residual, SSCTR-P34-F03. Its restart has no scientific justification (CL1). Separating it from X1 needs a partial-adherence criterion, which is a new count or threshold (G03 with Data, then the Founder), not existing authority.
Q2_IsolatedVersusConsistentTraining.bindingReading: BR-Q2: the direction-A trigger is BR-Q1.2(d). No adherence count, share, threshold, window or rolling week is added. An isolated, partial, aborted, conflicted or adverse session, or sessions in no whole plan week, never trigger direction A. Neither does a week whose only re-entry-complete sport has no required session (BR-Q4.4).
Q2_IsolatedVersusConsistentTraining.holdoutScoring: Recommendation to the Founder, who decides under CF-P33-03. On X2's exact path (no plan week wholly between is re-entry-complete in any sport), a continuity restart is the disclosed residual of this record, not a domain failure. These are domain failures: (i) a restart or continuity reading where some sport had a re-entry-complete week wholly between (the inverse defect direction A closes); (ii) a return that drops an earlier break's effect without such a week (F01); (iii) on X2's path, any outcome other than continuity, because it would reveal an unauthorized partial-adherence rule.

Q3_PerSport.verdict: Gamma is accepted and M is rejected. A sport with its own whole re-entry-complete week between reads its executed history; the other sport reads from x's reconstructed return. M couples running to strength: X3 and X3c differ only in one strength session, yet under M running falls from EASY 70 to RETURN step 1 at 45. Under gamma, running in X3 equals X3c, the full re-entry outcome, which is what Front B asks. A strength data gap (unlogged reps or reps in reserve, a load in an unknown unit) or a missed lift holds only the strength conclusion. No scientific dependency (CL4; L8, L10 weighed) and no technical dependency justifies holding running for it. Evidence about one sport never moves another (I10/I11); the composition still coordinates the two sports.

bindingReading.BR-Q3.1_perSport: Under OWN_RETURN, the state of each sport s at the current stop's start is taken as follows. If s has its own candidate week re-entry-complete for s, it is the state without the reconstruction, read as in full re-entry. Otherwise it is the reducer's state with the reconstruction in force from its point. The two sports may re-enter in different weeks; when both have their own week, both read the executed history, at the full re-entry doses, labelled OWN_RETURN.
bindingReading.BR-Q3.2_couplingsKept: Only these existing couplings remain, and nothing else. (1) The systemic rule: converging adverse responses across sports, or in three or more sessions, hold every gate, so neither sport is re-entry-complete. (2) Clinical first: any clinical signal routes both. (3) The current stop has one return class for both sports (one class per return, R6). (4) The trigger itself: whether the sport without its own week reads x's own return or the continuous stop depends on whether the other sport re-entered (SSCTR-P34-F03, disclosed).
bindingReading.BR-Q3.3_load: The combined load after the return never exceeds the combination the athlete executed. The re-entered sport resumes executed doses; the other resumes at x's own return or below. The existing hybrid composition (arrangement, spacing, key-session protection) applies unchanged to the weeks it plans.

Q4_ReentryWeekContract.verdict: One reading binds the runtime, P18(a), the pre-registration and the public contract. It applies to full re-entry and to direction A's trigger alike. Neither present text is right as it stands. The runtime must add RACE_TOUCH and RACE. INTERFACE-5, PREREG-5 Delta 1 and Delta 2 and P18(a) must drop the optional ungated sessions. A sport re-enters only through the sessions that carry its prescribed training stimulus. Sessions the plan itself marks optional are an equal alternative by design, so their absence says nothing about tolerance. On R7D-FREEZE-4 a race week with the race and the touch missed re-enters running on one 25-minute easy run (W4, TRAINING_AFTER). That is the F01 pattern on a race week, and with RACE_KEYS it becomes OWN_RETURN.

bindingReading.BR-Q4.1_runRequired: Running, required: every live run session of the week with role EASY, LONG, QUALITY or WALK_JOG (the gated roles, read as the reducer gates them), RACE_TOUCH and RACE. Each must be executed as prescribed. For a gated role that means a completed, non-conflicted, non-substituted report meeting the existing completion rule, with its gate ADVANCE or EARNED, so no adverse or conflicting response. For RACE_TOUCH it means the same report test and no adverse or conflicting response, read as the gate rule reads a gated row. For RACE it means the race finished: completed and not conflicted; the event window is not a target (R7-A), and no adverse or conflicting response is reported. The WALK_JOG the plan marks optional after a race is gated by the reducer and so counts as required. That is a disclosed conservative exception, rare (walk/jog athletes in a post-event week), and kept so that one predicate serves both step release and re-entry.
bindingReading.BR-Q4.2_runNotRequired: Running, not required: WALK (the optional brisk walk), RECOVERY_EASY (optional after the race), SHAKEOUT (optional the day before the race) and optional strides inside an easy run. A missed or unreported optional session never blocks re-entry. An executed one adds no re-entry evidence. An adverse response reported on it counts only through the existing systemic rule (BR-Q3.2).
bindingReading.BR-Q4.3_strength: Strength, required: every live strength session of the week, and in it every prescribed exercise, with its gate ADVANCE or EARNED and a usable deciding log: reps logged, reps in reserve logged, and a load in a known unit or bodyweight. This is the reducer's complete(STRENGTH). A missing or unusable log holds only strength (BR-Q3).
bindingReading.BR-Q4.4_sportPlanned: A sport re-enters only through a week that holds at least one required session of that sport. For full re-entry, every sport the week plans (any live session, optional included) must have re-entered through that week. A week whose running is only optional therefore re-enters strength alone, and running reads x's own return.
bindingReading.BR-Q4.5_unchanged: Weeks are the plan's own weeks. SKIPPED sessions are handled as now (a skip without a move keeps its MISSED row). A week a review closed re-enters only by this same test. No phase is excluded, because doses stay capped at executed (O-01). No count, threshold or length is added.

BR-Q4.6_ruling_per_role.WALK_JOG: required (the optional post-event walk/jog included, as gated)

Q5_StatedStartOnTheLaterBreaksFirstDay.verdict: Yes, the QRE's EXP-1 reading. With a stated start time, a plan week whose last session falls on the later break's first day, and was executed before that time, lies wholly between. The record orders the session before the stop, as the existing startedAt rule (0.8) and stateAtBreak's history cut already do. Prototype with P34_SAME_DAY=1: S1 (the Sunday long run at 08:00, the trip from 18:00) re-enters, TRAINING_AFTER, SHORT 4, where FREEZE-4 gives MODERATE 24. S2 (the same run reported at 19:00, after the start) does not re-enter running: strength re-enters by its own week, OWN_RETURN, and running reads x's return.
Q5_StatedStartOnTheLaterBreaksFirstDay.bindingReading: BR-Q5: a session dated on S counts as before the stop only when S has a stated start time and the session has an executed report observed before it. That is the history cut at startedAt, so the reducer reads such a week as complete or not. A session on S that is unreported, not done, or executed after the start makes its week not re-entry-complete; it does not fall outside the week. Without a stated start time, S is read as wholly inside the break (0.8), unchanged. A session on the earlier break's last day is inside that break; no end time exists in the contract. The test author covers S1, S2, and both boundary days with and without startedAt (QE-R7D-P33-05).

Q6_AdverseResponses.verdict: Yes. An adverse response (recovery ADVERSE, next-day function IMPAIRED) is a training-response signal: the executed dose was not tolerated as planned. So it is the right input for direction A. An adverse run holds the run gate, so running is not re-entry-complete (C4: running reads x's return held at RETURN 20/30/30/45, strength reads its own complete week). A systemic signal holds both sports: no sport is re-entry-complete, and continuity follows (X6: MODERATE 25 RETURN 20/30/30/45, the same doses as ANY's SHORT 4). It is not a clinical route by itself. Pain, illness, injury, a functional limitation or a clinical eligibility flag route first, before any reconstruction, unchanged.
Q6_AdverseResponses.bindingReading: BR-Q6: the trigger and the per-sport reading use the reducer's gates unchanged, including the systemic rule. An adverse or conflicting response on a required session makes its sport not re-entry-complete for that week. Clinical first is checked before any reading of the training between (every break, the review's eligibility).

Q7_Invariants.verdict: Gamma's outcomes respect the invariants on every path probed, except two, both pre-existing, which gamma reaches or carries. SSCTR-P34-F01 credits missed runs in the single-run ceiling, so a dose rises above what was executed. SSCTR-P34-F02 drops earlier breaks on a named correction of the latest one. Both are preconditions for freezing the direction-A candidate (CF-P34-02, CF-P34-03).

perInvariant.executedHistoryNeverErased: Respected. Every report stays on record. The re-entered sport reads it. The other sport reads x's return plus the facts after it, and its executed loads are kept as facts (O-06).
perInvariant.missedTrainingNeverCredited: Respected by the re-entry logic: no step without a closed or complete week, no catch-up. Violated by the pre-existing SSCTR-P34-F01 when a return is re-planned from its own week.
perInvariant.noCalendarOnlyProgression: Respected: return steps are conditional on executed weeks, and x's reconstructed return is never progressed by date.
perInvariant.noReturnAboveAuthorizedCapacity: Respected: doses are capped at executed (historicalRun) and by the single-run ceiling, once SSCTR-P34-F01 is fixed. Full re-entry after a low-load week can resume pre-break doses within the ceiling (O-01, pre-existing, accepted).
perInvariant.runningAndStrengthCoordinated: Respected through the composition, the systemic coupling and the combined-load property (BR-Q3.3). The trigger coupling is disclosed (SSCTR-P34-F03).
perInvariant.I9_identitiesAndEvents: Respected: no break is joined, no declaration is edited, and the reconstruction is never recorded as a fact (BR-Q1.4). The correction path is broken pre-existing (SSCTR-P34-F02).
perInvariant.clinicalFirst: Respected: C1-C3 and X7 are identical on every variant; clinical routing precedes any reconstruction.

addendumRuling.question: After a return that read separate breaks, must a named correction of the latest break re-read the separate breaks that return recorded, by the same rules, and is that within existing authority?
addendumRuling.ruling: Yes, and yes. A named correction supersedes only the report it corrects, the latest break (I1, I3, I9). It changes none of the earlier breaks' facts and none of the training between them. So the stop it reads must be re-derived from the corrected latest break together with the separate breaks the corrected return recorded (its separateBreaks rows, whose declarations are still on the carried record), by the same rules as the first return (BR-Q1, BR-Q4, BR-Q5). The corrected dates can change their relation: overlap, touch, or a whole week now in or out. That re-derivation reads it. Authority used: I9; R7-A.1 C5 and R7-A.2 I9 (a newer report of the same break replaces only that break's own adaptations; a separate break's stay with it); the Phase 3.2/3.3 rule that a later break never erases an earlier one's effect; and BR-Q1. No number. This is not later-mission work. It is the F01 defect re-entering by the correction path, and the Founder's Phase 3.4 invariants for front A name corrections explicitly. Classification: SSCTR-P34-F02 (pre-existing, safety-relevant). Binding before the direction-A candidate is frozen; if Chief or the Founder rule it out of this phase, it blocks any final holdout.
addendumRuling.evidence: C1 on R7D-FREEZE-4 and on the prototype: the F1 shape returns MODERATE 21 (EASY 15, LONG 20, then 30/30/45). The trip, named and corrected to 5 days, then gives SHORT 5 resuming EASY 34, LONG 65, THRESHOLD 41, LONG 70, the pre-holiday doses with quality, which is F01 itself. C2 on the prototype: the V1 shape returns SHORT 4 with x OWN_RETURN. The correction then gives SHORT 5 with strength at back-squat 2x8@85 instead of x's own return entry (1x7 ESTABLISH), so x's effect on strength is dropped.
addendumRuling.relatedObservation: A correction naming the earlier, consumed separate break is asked (C3: ASK interruption.episodeId on both runtimes). That fails closed, a usability residual with QE-R7D-P33-03 (O-02).

Q7_Invariants.staleReturnRuling: The coordinator's addendum fact 1 (a spurious late-evidence question after an OWN_RETURN return) is an engineering defect of the prototype. The announced fix is the right domain reading: every recomputation of that return uses the same reading, rebuilt from the return's own record. Condition: the fix must not suppress a genuine late-evidence question. Training before the later break, recorded after the return and not read by it, is still asked (I6, confirmation-first). Test both (CF-P34-04).

Q8_F08SportingProcessAfterClearance.verdict: No part of F08 is approvable or implementable now. The clearance contract, its issuer classes, restriction vocabulary and stop signs, and the decision that a nonclinical recipe is adequate after a given condition are clinical (G04, DR-99, SSCTR-02/05/06); no qualified owner exists in the project. The sporting process is described below as a candidate reading of which existing rules could serve S6 inside a valid clearance. It is not approved and it authorizes nothing. F08 stays open. Runna's three return speeds are a UX reference only: rejected as dose options (uncalibrated choices; the engine has one recipe per class).

clinical_CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED: whether the athlete may train at all (return to participation), in which sport, with which restrictions, and for how long the clearance is valid
what a qualified clearance is: issuer, verification, scope, dates (with PCG and Security for the form and the trust boundary)
the stop signs that end the return and send the athlete back to assessment, and their vocabulary

whether the nonclinical return recipe is adequate for this condition at all, or a condition-specific progression is needed (for example after a respiratory infection, L13, or a return-to-running programme after injury, L14)
whether training one cleared sport is safe for a condition affecting the other
re-assessment after any recurrence; interpretation of symptoms; any reading of an adverse response as a symptom
nonclinical_candidate_for_SSCTR_after_G0: the training-dose mechanics inside a valid clearance's scope and restrictions, using only existing rules: start from current capacity, never the pre-break plan; the return class by the clinical break's own length, by the unchanged table, as a floor never shortened (the proposal's candidate, the most conservative existing recipe); a current demonstration where the recipe uses one, read as a dose input only, never as evidence of healing; prior tolerated doses as a ceiling, never a target by date; executed-evidence-gated progression, no catch-up, MEC
per sport: a sport NOT_CLEARED stays held, with no prescription and the record kept; the cleared sport proceeds through the existing composition; no cross-sport safety is inferred
restrictions applied as hard caps that no coach, volume or difficulty profile overrides; only when G04's closed vocabulary maps them to existing plan elements deterministically, otherwise ASK
the transition applied alone (breakCarrierAsk, event separation); history and the original clinical reason kept; a later nonclinical break never clears or overwrites a clinical one
theLine.sendBackToQualifiedAssessment: Existing triggers, unchanged: any clinical eligibility flag (pain, persistent pain, injury, illness, functional limitation, clinical concern), a clinical reason or mention in any new break or substitution, an unclear answer (ASK), and any stop sign the clearance lists. Abstention: whether an adverse or impaired response during S6 is a training response or a symptom is a clinical classification. Until G04 defines stop signs, the conservative reading is to ask and route it, never to treat it only as a training hold. This is not a new criterion; it is the existing next-observation text ('any pain, illness or abnormal symptom routes to qualified assessment').
theLine.runningVersusStrength: Only the scope the clearance states is prescribed. A sport absent from the scope or NOT_CLEARED is held under CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED. The cleared sport's class comes from the clinical break's own days, its entry from the unchanged recipe, its steps from its own executed evidence (R40). Strength restrictions (a body region, a movement) need G04's vocabulary before the catalog can exclude or substitute anything. Without it, ASK.

Q8_F08SportingProcessAfterClearance.existingRulesThatCouldServeS6: Reassessment: the eligibility gate (NONCLINICAL_CONFIRMED, every flag false, assessed on or after the clearance). The return class by the break's own length (R6 table). The current demonstration (operational.return.demonstration). Prior doses as ceiling (historicalRun; returnLoadCap; strengthKnownLoadAfterReturnLog). The single-run ceiling, once SSCTR-P34-F01 is fixed. The reducer's evidence-gated steps. The R6 restart run-history clearing for long breaks. Each is a candidate only, subject to G04's decision that it is adequate for the condition.
Q8_F08SportingProcessAfterClearance.blocker: Owner: G04 qualified professionals (clinical content), PCG and Founder (authority form, Part 2), Security (before any clearance input enters the runtime). Reopening trigger: an approved G04 clearance contract and authority form, and a Security review of the input. Then a fresh SSCTR review of the S6 sporting mechanics within it.

findings.class: PRE_EXISTING_RUNTIME_DEFECT (aggressive direction, safety-relevant); reached by direction A on a new path
findings.new: Not found in the R7-D phase records I searched. Reproduced on R7D-FREEZE-4 with a single break.
findings.finding: When a return is re-planned from its own week (fromWeek = the decision's week, a report on Wednesday or later), the single-run ceiling of the weeks after it counts that week's elapsed run sessions as executed. That holds when they were unreported, reported not done, or inside the declared stop. The policy reads the ceiling from 'the longest completed run ... from the completed-work ledger; in a conditional projection, earlier projected weeks count as executed'. Elapsed sessions of the decision's own week are neither completed nor projected.
findings.reproduction: ssctr-probes/p34-ceiling.mjs, identical on both runtimes. A 21-day break (Mon wk4 to Sun wk6), weeks 2-3 not done, so no completed run in the 30 days before week 7. G1 (Monday report): wk7 15/15/15, wk8 20/20/20, wk9 25/25/25. G2/G3/G4 (Wednesday or Friday report; elapsed week-7 runs unreported or reported not done): wk8 EASY 30, EASY 30, LONG 45; wk9 EASY 45, THRESHOLD 34, LONG 55. Direction A: R1 (14-day holiday; 3 weeks with strength done and every run not done; trip Mon-Thu wk7; plain review Fri wk7) on the prototype gives SHORT 4, running RETURN LONG 15, then 30/30/45, then EASY 45/34 and LONG 60 in week 9, after about 45 days with no completed run. R7D-FREEZE-4 gives LONG 39 RESTART 15/20/20/20 on R1. The same facts planned from a whole week ahead (G5) give 15/20/25 on the prototype.
findings.assessment: This credits missed training and plans doses and quality above the facts ceiling. Direction A does not create it, but on R1 it turns a restart into an aggressive return. The ruling uses existing policy text only; no number.
findings.routeTo: Chief, then Engineering (fix) under Founder authorization. Within front A's invariants ('missed training never credited', 'no return above authorized capacity'), or a separate authorization. Binding before the direction-A candidate is frozen (CF-P34-03); before any final holdout in every case.

findings.class: PRE_EXISTING_RUNTIME_DEFECT (F01 direction, safety-relevant); coordinator's addendum fact 2, confirmed
findings.finding: After a return that read separate breaks, a named correction of the latest break re-reads that break alone. The earlier breaks were consumed by the first return and are not episodes, so their effect is dropped.
findings.reproduction: ssctr-probes/p34-ssctr.mjs. C1 (R7D-FREEZE-4 and prototype): MODERATE 21, then the trip corrected to 5 days gives SHORT 5 resuming EASY 34, LONG 65, THRESHOLD 41, LONG 70. C2 (prototype): SHORT 4 with x OWN_RETURN, then the correction gives SHORT 5 with back-squat 2x8@85 instead of x's return entry.
findings.ruling: Q7 addendumRuling: re-read the corrected return's separate breaks by the same rules; existing authority; no number.
findings.routeTo: Chief, then Engineering. In scope of front A (corrections intact). Binding before freeze (CF-P34-02).

findings.finding: Two parts. (1) X2 path: when no plan week wholly between is re-entry-complete in any sport (both sports partial every week), gamma keeps continuity: LONG 32 RESTART for weeks of near-full training. That has no scientific justification (CL1). (2) The trigger couples the sport without its own week to the other sport. V2 and X2 run identically, yet running gives RETURN 20/30/30/45 in V2 (strength complete) against RESTART 15/20/20/20 in X2 (strength partial).
findings.assessment: Over-conservative, not unsafe. Separating X2 from X1 (isolated) needs a partial-adherence criterion, a new count or threshold, so it is not existing authority. Per-sport return classes would be option (b), not authorized. Reachable only on the bulk or late form (no weekly review applies the earlier break); weekly reviews avoid it (V4).
findings.routeTo: Founder/PCG with G03 and Data, if a partial-adherence criterion or per-sport return classes are wanted. Holdout scoring recommendation in Q2. Disclose without envelope (CF-P34-07).

findings.class: DOMAIN_RESIDUAL_NON_BLOCKING (less conservative for one sport; equals the existing episode rule)
findings.finding: When one sport triggers direction A, a sport with no executed session at all between x and the later stop (R1: running entirely not done while strength is complete) is read from x's own return. Its missed weeks count as missed sessions (holds), not as a continuous stop for that sport. Running gets x's MODERATE re-entry (achieved peaks kept) where its de facto 39-day lapse would class LONG (restart, peaks cleared). The same holds today in the timely path: an applied MODERATE return followed by weeks of missed runs (R1k).
findings.assessment: Strength work does not maintain running adaptations (CL5), so for running this is less conservative than the physiology. Once SSCTR-P34-F01 is fixed, it is bounded by the existing single-run ceiling (G5: 15/20/25 per week from the entry) and by evidence-gated steps. Remaining differences from a restart: achieved peaks kept, so taper and race-week doses come from pre-break peaks within the ceiling, and quality can return after the conditional return steps. Accepted only with SSCTR-P34-F01 fixed. Reading the lapse as a long stop for that sport alone would need per-sport return classes (option b).
findings.routeTo: Founder/PCG with the per-sport return-class question (NF-R7AB-1 / R40 family), which already covers the episode rule's missed-weeks behaviour. Disclose (CF-P34-07).

findings.finding: The runtime's re-entry predicate omits RACE_TOUCH and RACE (W2-W4 on R7D-FREEZE-4: a race week with the race and the touch missed re-enters running on one 25-minute easy run). INTERFACE-5, PREREG-5 Delta 1 and Delta 2 and P18(a) require optional ungated sessions (QH-1 false block). Neither matches BR-Q4.
findings.routeTo: Chief and the interface/instrument owner. Runtime: add RACE_TOUCH and RACE (BR-Q4.1). Instrument: P18(a) per BR-Q4, plus the OWN_RETURN semantics, with no oracle weakening (CF-P34-05).

observations.note: Full re-entry after a low-load week (pre-existing, accepted). L1: holiday, then a consolidation week executed in full (LONG 65), then a trip. SHORT 4 resumes LONG 70, executed before the holiday and within the single-run ceiling, on both runtimes. The episode rule gives RETURN 20/35/35/45. Doses stay within executed capacity and the ceiling; disclose; no change.
A correction naming an earlier separate break that a return consumed is asked (C3: ASK interruption.episodeId). Fails closed; a usability residual with QE-R7D-P33-03.
The prototype's spurious staleReturn question after an OWN_RETURN return is engineering (coordinator's fact 1); see the Q7 staleReturnRuling.

The M variant planned THRESHOLD 34 within its first week after a MODERATE 11-day stop on X8 (its virtual return already in RETURN mode). Not investigated further: M is rejected, and on R7D-FREEZE-4 a second moderate break during a return re-enters at step 0 (checked in scratch).

The reconstructed return uses the current review's eligibility and infers none for the past. It prescribes nothing retroactively, so no historical assessment is needed. Clinical signals on record still route first.

On X5, the strength sport read from x's own return starts the return steps from the state at x's start: back-squat entry from 82.5 kg, prescribed as 1x7 ESTABLISH. It does not adopt the 85 kg executed after x in incomplete weeks. Conservative; the existing recipe.

aeReview.1_planAdequate: No. Two declared stops make the pre-break plan stale; it is never restored by date.
aeReview.2_materialFact: Yes. Two declared breaks with provenance, and the executed sessions between them with their gates, append-only.
aeReview.3_keepDefensible: No. Ignoring the earlier break (F01) or counting real training as stop days (P33-F01) both misread the record.
aeReview.4_changeNecessary: Yes. The return depends on which sport, if any, showed tolerance in a whole plan week after the earlier break.
aeReview.5_smallestIntervention: The unchanged recipe for the later stop by its own days, from the per-sport state the record supports: executed history for a re-entered sport, the earlier break's own return for the other. Continuity only when no sport re-entered.
aeReview.6_smallerAlternatives: ANY reopens isolated sessions as resumption (CL2). M penalizes running for strength gaps (Front B, CL4). A partial-adherence criterion would be a new threshold.
aeReview.7_priorityAndProgression: Prior tolerated doses stay the ceiling. No progression is invented. Progression is restored on V1-type paths. A cost remains on X2 (F03).
aeReview.8_evidenceSupportsDose: Classes and doses are the approved R6 policy, unchanged. Direction-only support, SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS (CL1-CL6).
aeReview.9_uncertainty: Individual detraining is not predictable from group means. The X2 and R1 residuals. The frequency of the bulk or late form depends on consumer design.
aeReview.10_askHoldClinical: ASK for unknown training between, unclear reasons and the relation of unnamed breaks. CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for any clinical break or flag before any reconstruction. F08 stays clinical.

newPrescriptiveAuthority: None. No new dose, threshold, count, length, percentage, ceiling, increment, tolerance, cadence, recipe or clinical criterion. Relative to R7D-FREEZE-4, prescribed training changes only where an earlier separate break is unapplied and some sport has a whole re-entry-complete plan week between it and the later break. There the later break is read by its own days from the per-sport state the earlier break's own return and the executed record give. Also: race weeks need their touch and race to re-enter running, and a same-day stated start orders a session executed before it.

One reading binds four places: the runtime, P18(a), a PREREG-5 addendum (or PREREG-6) and an INTERFACE delta. It covers the re-entry contract (BR-Q4), OWN_RETURN and ownReturn per sport (BR-Q1.4), the per-sport reading (BR-Q3) and the same-day rule (BR-Q5). The F01 detectors stay. Add an inverse-defect detector: a continuity reading (TRAINING_NOT_REESTABLISHED or NO_TRAINING_BETWEEN) while a qualifying week exists in some sport fails. It must flag R7D-FREEZE-4 on V1/X5. Add false-block controls: QH-1 (optional walks not done); a race week with its touch or race missed, which must not count as re-entry for running; a week in full without reps in reserve, which re-enters running alone; S1 and S2. The SSCTR-P32-F01 sensitivity rows stay detected. The oracle is never weakened.

Directed tests, in addition to QE-R7D-P33-05's list. X1-X8, V1-V5, E4, C4, X6 and X7. R1, R1b, R2, L1, the W1-W4 race weeks, S1/S2, C1-C3. A run-only and a strength-only plan. Three breaks with recursion (X8). Each sport re-entering in a different week. An applied return between the breaks (the guard). Timely comparators V4 and K unchanged.

Disclose without envelope in the freeze record, the handoff and the pre-registration: SSCTR-P34-F03 (X2 continuity restart; trigger coupling), SSCTR-P34-F04 (a sport lapse read as missed sessions), O-01, the QE-R7D-P33-03 guard and O-02. Consumer conditions, added to CF-P33-04 and PREREG-5 Delta 11. (a) Explain per sport: which sport resumed at the doses executed and from which week, and which resumed from the earlier break's own return. Never say the earlier break 'did not count'. (b) Present OWN_RETURN as the earlier break applied when the athlete came back. (c) Add no number of your own.
